t.3.52.1: Bṛhadaśva said: Having promised them, "I will do it," O Bhārata, Nala then stood with joined palms and questioned them.
t.3.52.2: Who indeed are you, sirs, and who is he whose messenger you wish me to be? And what must I do there? Tell me this truly.
t.3.52.3: When the Naiṣadha had spoken thus, Maghavān replied: "Know us to be immortals, come here for the sake of Damayantī."
t.3.52.4: I am Indra, this is Agni, and likewise this is the Lord of the Waters; and this, O king, is Yama, who brings an end to the bodies of men.
t.3.52.5: So you, then, announce to Damayantī that we have come: “The World-Guardians, together with Indra, are coming to you, eager to see you.”
t.3.52.6: The gods Śakra, Agni, Varuṇa and Yama wish to win you. Choose one of these gods to be your husband.
t.3.52.7: Thus addressed by Śakra, Nala, with joined palms, said: "I have come here with that very same purpose; you should not send me."
t.3.52.8: Having earlier promised us, "I will do it," O Naiṣadha, why will you not do it? Go, O Naiṣadha, without delay!
t.3.52.9: Bṛhadaśva said: Thus addressed by those gods, the Naiṣadha spoke again: "How can I venture to enter dwellings that are so well guarded?"
t.3.52.10: "You will enter," Śakra said to him once more. Saying "So be it," he went to the dwelling of Damayantī.
t.3.52.11: There he saw the princess of Vidarbha, surrounded by a throng of her friends, the fair-complexioned lady blazing forth with her beauty of form and her splendor.
t.3.52.12: She was exceedingly delicate of limb, slender-waisted and fair-eyed, and seemed by her own radiance to cast aside the splendour of the moon.
t.3.52.13: As soon as he saw her of the lovely smile, his desire swelled; but, wishing to keep his word true, he held back the love that lay in his heart.
t.3.52.14: Then those most excellent women, seeing the Naiṣadha, sprang up from their seats in agitation, overpowered by his splendor.
t.3.52.15: And those women, greatly delighted and filled with wonder, praised Nala; yet they did not speak to him, but only honored him in their minds.
t.3.52.16: Oh, the beauty! Oh, the radiance! Oh, the composure of this great-souled one! Who can he be: a god, a Yakṣa, or a Gandharva?
t.3.52.17: But they could not say anything at all to him; all those bashful, lovely women were overpowered by his splendor.
t.3.52.18: Then Damayantī, who was wont to speak with a smile, as though smiling and filled with wonder, addressed the heroic Nala.
t.3.52.19: Who are you, O you of flawless limbs, who increase the love in my heart? You have come here like an immortal, O hero; I wish to know about you, O sinless one.
t.3.52.20: How did you come here, and how is it that you were not seen? For my palace is well guarded, and the king is stern in his commands.
t.3.52.21: Thus addressed by the princess of Vidarbha, Nala replied to her: "Know me to be Nala, O lovely one, come here as the messenger of the gods."
t.3.52.22: The gods wish to win you: Śakra, Agni, Varuṇa and Yama. Choose one of those gods as your husband, O lovely one.
t.3.52.23: By their power alone I entered unnoticed; for no one saw me as I was entering, nor did anyone hold me back.
t.3.52.24: For this purpose, gentle lady, I have been sent by the best of the gods. Having heard this, auspicious one, make up your mind as you wish.
